description: Observe an existing durable run (or a queued job id) through bounded event replay. Defaults: afterSeq=0, waitMs=25000, maxEvents=50, wake=batch. Events already available at the snapshot fence are returned first, even while a question is pending. wake=batch then keeps collecting until the page fills, it includes a question event (also one written before the wait), the run ends, or waitMs elapses; wake=event returns as soon as any event is available. waitMs=0 returns only the already available page. A pending question whose event is not in the page never ends a wait by itself; it is always reported in pendingInteractions. Resume with nextSeq; snapshotSeq is a fence, and terminal is not the end of events, until a page with no events reports eventOmission stream_ended (the stream cannot serve the rest, such as a last line left unterminated by a crash): stop there. Pages are capped at 64 KiB of events, pending bodies at 32 KiB, results at 128 KiB (UTF-8 JSON); an event too large for any page is named in oversizedEvent: read it with claudexor_run_event_read, then resume with afterSeq set to its seq. Daemon discovery and each snapshot read have separate 5s budgets, so a call can take waitMs plus about 15s; size waitMs to your client's tool timeout. Timeout, disconnect and host abort close only this read, never the worker. Use claudexor_run_result for output and claudexor_run_interactions for omitted question bodies.

afterSeq.description: Last durable event seq already consumed (the previous nextSeq), never snapshotSeq.

runId.description: Run id, or the job id of an accepted launch that may still be queued.

waitMs.description: Bound of the event stage. Zero never waits for new events: it returns the bounded page already available at the snapshot fence, read within a separate 5s budget. Daemon discovery and each snapshot read have their own 5s budgets, so one call can take up to waitMs plus about 15s.

wake.description: batch (default): collect events until the page fills, it includes a question event (interaction.requested, also one written before the wait), the run ends, or waitMs elapses. event: return as soon as any event is available. A pending question whose event is not in the page is reported in both modes but never ends a wait by itself.

name: claudexor_run_wait

outputSchema.description: Read-only run observation, at most 131072 UTF-8 JSON bytes: at most two snapshot reads and one stream subscription, no automatic reconnect or worker cancellation. Events already available at the snapshot fence are returned before any wait, whether or not a question is pending. Resume with nextSeq.

eventOmission.description: Why the page stopped early: event_limit or byte_limit (more events may follow; resume with nextSeq), oversized_frame (the next frame exceeds the 131072-byte stream frame cap), invalid_event (the next frame failed validation and is never skipped), stream_ended (the stream, which ends only for a terminal run, served nothing after nextSeq although snapshotSeq is higher, such as a last line left unterminated by a crash; nothing was skipped, and the same call returns the same page until the log changes, so stop there). Null means no limit was reached, not that replay is exhausted.

events.description: Ordered new events, at most 65536 UTF-8 JSON bytes including envelopes. Legacy events retain their body and use the stream id as seq.

event.description: Append-only run event record (one JSONL line in the run's event log).

seq.description: Monotonic per-run sequence stamped at emit time; the durable SSE cursor and snapshot fence. Optional only for pre-v0.8.0 artifacts.

thread_id.description: Thread this run is a turn of, when any.

type.description: Type of an append-only run event, covering run lifecycle, contract/context creation, budget, routing fallbacks, harness activity, interactions, gates, review, arbitration, work products, and control verbs.

nextSeq.description: Last returned event seq, or afterSeq when none was returned. It never advances over an unreturned event.

seq.description: Durable seq of the next unread event.

type.description: Event type the daemon stream names for it.

oversizedEvent.description: The next unread event after nextSeq cannot fit one page. Read its exact bytes in parts with claudexor_run_event_read, then resume with afterSeq set to its seq. Null otherwise.

pendingInteractions.description: Current snapshot's pending questions, bounded to 32768 UTF-8 JSON bytes; claudexor_run_interactions returns complete bodies. They never hold back events.

items.description: A live interactive question awaiting the user's answer (snapshot projection).

attemptId.description: Attempt the interaction was raised in, when known.

items.description: One question of an interactive user-input request.

header.description: Short chip/header text some harnesses attach to a question.

multi_select.description: Whether multiple options may be selected.

options.description: Selectable options; empty for free-text-only questions.

items.description: One multiple-choice option of an interactive question.

description.description: Optional longer explanation of the option.

label.description: Option label shown to the user.

sourceTool.description: Native tool that raised the request.

timeoutAt.description: When the interaction times out into a benign decline; null = no timeout.

runId.description: Canonical run id; a queued job id converges to its run id once the run binds.

snapshotProblem.description: A failed final read leaves the explicitly labelled initial snapshot, never invented current state.

snapshotSeq.description: Last event seq at the latest snapshot: a fence, not a cursor. nextSeq below it means events are already written; eventOmission stream_ended reports when the stream cannot serve them.

status.description: Control-plane run state = the run LIFECYCLE (D8): queued/running while live, then exactly one of succeeded / failed / cancelled / interrupted. Outcome quality (checks/review/delivery) is orthogonal — see outcomeFacts.

wakeReason.description: Why this observation returned, by precedence: aborted (this read was cancelled; the worker continues), terminal (the run is terminal; events may still follow nextSeq unless eventOmission is stream_ended), interactions (this page includes a question event), events (event mode, a completed zero-wait page, or a page, even an empty one, stopped by event_limit, byte_limit, oversized_frame or invalid_event), timeout (waitMs elapsed, possibly with a partial batch), disconnected (the stream ended early; never completion).
